html:
Denmark was a pioneer of modern wind power. After the oil crises of the 1970s it built wind turbines on a large scale, and wind now gives about half of its electricity.

Danish engineers had experimented with wind electricity since the 1890s. The oil shock of 1973 hit a country that imported almost all its energy, and a popular movement rejected nuclear power. Cooperatives of local people bought small turbines, and state support helped firms such as Vestas grow.

In 1991 Denmark built Vindeby, the first offshore wind farm. Danish companies remain among the largest turbine makers and offshore wind builders in the world. The shift is part of Denmark's aim to stop burning fossil fuels, and of the global fight against climate change.
sum: Denmark was a pioneer of modern wind power. After the oil crises of the 1970s it built wind turbines on a large scale, and wind now gives about half of its electricity.
